This Civil Miscellaneous Appeal has been filed by the appellants challenging the quantum of compensation granted by the Tribunal in the award dated 06.10.2021 made in M.C.O.P.No.124 of 2018 on the file of the Special District Judge, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Salem.

sentences.text: 2.The appellants filed M.C.O.P. No.124 of 2018 on the file of the Special District Judge, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Salem claiming a sum of Rs.1,00,00,000/- as compensation for the death of one Rajasekaran, who died in the accident that took place on 14.08.2017.

entities.text: Special District Judge, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Salem
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: _ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

3. According to the appellants, on 14.08.2017 at about 17.30 hours the deceased and the appellants were travelling in a car bearing Reg.No.TN 30-BC-3561 driven by one Dhandayuthapani from Madurai to Tuticorin main road in Eppothum Vendran near Odaikaruppan temple bridge, the driver of the car drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and hit against the centre median.
As a result, the said Rajesekar died in the spot and the appellants also sustained multiple grievous injuries.
The deceased was aged 44 years and was earning Rs.35,000/- per month as a Manager in Asian Paint Company at the time of the accident.

4. The 1st respondent filed a counter statement denying all the averments made by the appellants in the claim petition and stated that the driver of the 1st respondent had driving license at the time of accident; that the above car was duly insured with the 2 nd respondent at the time of accident and stated that the compensation claimed by the appellants is highly excessive and prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
_ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 5.

The 2nd respondent filed a counter statement denying all the averments made by the appellants in the claim petition and stated that the seating capacity of the car was five (including the driver),
but six persons travelled in the above car, at the time of accident; that there is a policy violation on the part of the 1st respondent and the 2nd respondent was not liable to pay the compensation; that the 1st respondent had no valid license at the time of the accident and stated that the compensation claimed by the appellants is highly excessive and prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
6. Before the Tribunal, the 1st appellant examined herself as PW1 and marked 44 documents as Exs.P.1 to P.44.
The respondents neither marked any document nor examined any witness on their side.

The reports of the medical board were marked as Ex.C.1 and Ex.C.2.
7.

The Tribunal after considering the evidence and documents filed on the side of the appellants held that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the car belonging to Thenmozhi vs V.Govindaraji on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148887801/
2
the first respondent and _____ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis directed the respondents 1 and 2 are jointly and severally to pay a sum of Rs.25,31,251/- as compensation to the appellants.
8.Aggrieved by the said order, the appellants have preferred the present appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.

9. The learned counsel for the appellants submitted that compensation awarded by the Tribunal is meagre; that based on the Income Tax Returns/Ex.P5 of the deceased, the Tribunal had taken the net income of the deceased as notional income at Rs.2,55,670/- per annum and had not awarded future prospects at 25%; that the Tribunal further erred in deducting 1/3rd towards personal expenses and ought to have deducted 1/4th towards personal expenses since there were four dependents for the deceased; that the Tribunal had also not awarded Loss of Consortium at Rs.40,000/- each to the appellants 2 to 4 and awarded only Rs.20,000/- each; that the Tribunal had not awarded the compensation under the heads Loss of Estate and Travel Expenses and hence,
prayed for enhancement of compensation.
_ _ _ __ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 10.
Though notice has been served on the 1st respondent and his name has been printed in the cause list, none has entered an appearance on his behalf.
11. The learned counsel for the second respondent per contra, submitted that Tribunal had awarded just compensation under all heads.
12. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellants as well as second respondent and perused the materials available on record.

13. From the materials on record, this Court finds that the Tribunal had taken into consideration Ex.P.5/Income Tax returns for the year 2016  17 and arrived at the income of the deceased as Rs.2,55,670/- per annum.
There is no _____ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis infirmity in the said finding.
The deceased was aged 44 years at the time of accident, as per post-mortem certificate/Ex.P2.
The Tribunal however had not granted 25% enhancement towards future prospects.
Further, the Tribunal had wrongly deducted 1/3rd of his income towards personal expenses though there were four dependents.
Hence, 1/4th of his income has to be deducted towards his personal expenses.

Thus, by applying multiplier 14, adding 25% towards future prospects and deducting 1/4th towards personal expenses of the deceased, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head Loss of Income is calculated as follows:
Rs.2,55,670 + Rs.63,917.5 (Rs.255670 X 25%) X 14 X 3/4 = Rs.33,55,669/-
13.
The Tribunal had not awarded compensation under the head Loss of Parental Consortium to the appellants 2 to 4 who are the children of the deceased.

Hence, this Court awards a sum of Rs.1,20,000/-
Thenmozhi vs V.Govindaraji on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148887801/
3 (Rs.40,000/- each) towards loss of parental consortium to the appellants 2 to 4.

sentences.text: Hence, the compensation awarded under the head Loss of Love and _____ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Affection is setaside.
The appellants are also entitled to compensation under the heads Loss of Estate and Transport Charges.
Hence, this Court awards Rs.15,000/- and Rs.10,000/- respectively under those heads.
The Tribunal had awarded Rs.25,000/- towards funeral expenses which is on the higher side and same is reduced to Rs.15,000/-.
Thus, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced from Rs.25,31,253/- to Rs.35,55,669/-, break-up as follows -

4 . Funeral Expenses 25,000/- 15,000/- Reduce

5. Loss of Parental --- 1,20,000/- Grante  consortium  5. Loss of Estate --- 15,000/-/ Grante  6. Transport Charges --- 10,000/- Grante  _____ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis  Total 25,31,253/- 35,55,669/- Enhanc  by  Rs.10,24 14.

With the above modification, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal at Rs.25,31,253/- is hereby enhanced to Rs.35,55,669/-
together with interest at 7.5% per annum (excluding the default period, if any) from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

The respondents 1 and 2 are jointly and severally directed to deposit the award amount, now determined by this Court, less the amount already deposited, if any, within a period of six weeks from the date of a receipt of copy of this Judgment.
On such deposit, the 1 st appellant is permitted to withdraw her share of the award amount, less the amount if any, already withdrawn, on the basis of apportionment fixed by the Tribunal.

The share of the minor appellants 2 to 4, are directed to be deposited in any one of the Nationalised Bank till the minor appellants attain Thenmozhi vs V.Govindaraji on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148887801/
